headline: Debora fell at home on 2026-10-02 and has since declined in bathing and dressing independence, while her spouse and primary caregiver Kevin reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: Debora fell in the kitchen on 2026-10-02 while reaching for a cabinet. She had a left forearm skin tear, denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and fall risk was reassessed as high. On 2026-10-05 PT found her gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 10-02 nursing note and 10-05 PT evaluation (fall, skin tear, denial of head strike/LOC, high fall risk, TUG 19s, walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, twice weekly).

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing; she was independent at the last review. On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting her out of the tub, and she said she has been skipping showers for fear of slipping. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: OT note and home care aide note support all details: moderate assistance, independent at last review, hands-on help out of tub, skipping showers, and the recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep, and said he is worried about managing evenings alone. He requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches exactly: exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, respite request, and discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist added it to the blister pack on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks, and no recheck is documented in the notes provided. The new medication began about 3 weeks before the 2026-10-02 fall.
items.verifier_note: Start date 09-13, PHQ-9 14, pharmacist 09-15 blister pack, 4-week recheck all supported. No recheck appears in the provided notes. 09-13 to 10-02 is 19 days, about 3 weeks.

items.statement: PT and OT recommended a front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, tub transfer bench, handheld shower and more home care hours (2026-10-05 and 2026-10-26). The notes provided do not show whether any of these are in place. Follow-up nursing notes on 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-13 report no new concerns.
items.verifier_note: Recommendations and dates are supported. The 10-27 and 11-13 nursing notes say 'no new concerns', but they do not mention the equipment or services. The statement's framing of them as follow-up on those recommendations is not supported by the notes. Also, two separate 11-13 notes are cited, which is minor.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which started 2026-08-01. The last flu vaccine was on 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season false, season start 2026-08-01, and last flu vaccine 2026-04-25.

questions_for_team: Which PT and OT recommendations (walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, tub bench, handheld shower, added bathing hours) have been ordered or delivered, and who owns each?
Has the 4-week sertraline recheck happened, and how are her mood and PHQ-9 now? Should the team review the medication list in light of the fall?
What respite and evening support can be offered to Kevin, and when will the team follow up with him?
How will the team address Debora's fear of slipping and her skipped showers while the bathroom equipment is pending?
Should a flu vaccine be offered this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the prior review date; pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions/discharges in the window, including any for chest pain, COPD exacerbation, or heart-related symptoms given recent ischemic heart disease onset (2025-04-19).

Falls and fall-risk screen: any falls or near-falls in the window, injury from falls, and whether fall-risk assessment was done, noting fall risk from beta-blocker, new antidepressant, and chronic pain.

Sertraline (started 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms, PHQ-9 of 14): confirm the start date and dose, check for any follow-up PHQ-9 and its result, adherence, side effects (GI upset, sleep change, dizziness, falls, bleeding risk given concurrent clopidogrel), and whether a prescriber follow-up or recheck is scheduled. Flag for team discussion; do not recommend changes.
Mood and social engagement: review attendance at PACE day programs and any missed days, staff notes on mood, withdrawal, or anhedonia, and any suicidal ideation screening documented.

Cardiac medication review: confirm metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, simvastatin, and nitroglycerin spray are being taken as listed; check any new or stopped cardiac medications, recent blood pressure and heart rate trends (including orthostatic readings), and any chest pain episodes and nitroglycerin use logged.

Respiratory status: review COPD/chronic bronchitis symptoms, rescue albuterol use frequency, inhaler technique and adherence for fluticasone/salmeterol, oxygen saturation readings, and any exacerbation treatment such as steroids or antibiotics in the window.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+, and hypothyroidism): compare current weight with prior review, note change of 5% or more, and check appetite and dietary intake.
Thyroid and levothyroxine: confirm adherence and timing, check whether TSH was drawn when due and the result, and note any new symptoms suggesting thyroid imbalance.
Glycemic monitoring for prediabetes: check most recent A1c or fasting glucose and whether repeat testing is due in the window.

Pain and breast cancer history: review chronic pain scores, analgesic use and any new pain sites, and confirm breast cancer surveillance (imaging, oncology follow-up) is current and that no new oncology visits or treatment changes occurred.

Function, cognition, and caregiver: review ADL/IADL changes (bathing, dressing, transfers, mobility aids), cognitive screen results and any new confusion, caregiver status and strain, transportation, and care-plan items due in the window (reassessment, care-plan update, MDS or PACE-required assessments, and any allergy documentation, since no allergies are recorded).
